title: The bush that burned (Exodus 3:1–6)
hookLine: put off the shoes from thy feet, for the place is holy ground

lines: A PRINCE, A FUGITIVE, A SHEPHERD.
A BUSH THAT DOESN'T BURN UP.
cards: The baby from the basket grew up in Pharaoh's palace. Then, as a grown man, he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, killed the Egyptian, and ran for his life.
Now he's in the land of Midian, married, keeping his father-in-law's sheep. The book of Acts says forty years go by. A prince who became a fugitive who became a shepherd.

One day he leads the flock to the far side of the wilderness, to a mountain called Horeb, and out of the corner of his eye sees a bush on fire. Not strange in a desert, except this one keeps burning and doesn't burn up.

teach.b: First, Moses turns aside. I'll go over and see this great sight, he says, why the bush isn't burnt. That small detour is the hinge of his life.
When the Lord saw that he turned aside to look, the text says, God called to him out of the bush: Moses, Moses. And he answers, here I am. Second, the command.

teach.h: PUT OFF THE SHOES FROM THY FEET.
teach.b: Just this: "Come not nigh hither, put off the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground." It's the same dirt he crossed a minute ago with his sheep; what changed is who was there.
Third, the face. God says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob."
And Moses hides his face, afraid to look at God. Fourth, what Catholics see in the bush.
Christian writers, Gregory of Nyssa among them, read this fire that burns without consuming as a picture of Mary: God dwelling within her, and her virginity kept whole.

teach.h: THE BUSH UNBURNT: A PICTURE OF MARY.
teach.b: An old antiphon for January first, the feast of Mary, Mother of God, sings it: in the bush Moses saw unburnt, the Church recognizes her virginity preserved.
Some readers hear in the Hebrew word for bush, seneh, an echo of Sinai, where this story will lead.
And the shoes stay in Catholic practice too: on Good Friday, the Roman Missal allows the priest to take off his shoes before he comes forward to venerate the cross.

how: On Good Friday, the Roman Missal allows the priest to remove his chasuble and shoes before venerating the cross, and in Eastern Catholic churches the burning bush appears in icons of Mary, the Mother of God.

run back to camp to get help.
games.why: he says, I'll turn aside and see this great sight. and when God sees him turn aside, God calls him by name.

practice: If you can, slip off your shoes and feel the floor under your bare feet; if not, press your feet into the ground where you are.

Your kitchen or bedroom hasn't changed, but let it be the ground Moses stood on, and treat an ordinary floor with reverence. If you pray, simply say, here I am; if you don't, let the stillness be enough.

wordCard.voice: Seneh, the Hebrew word for the thornbush that burned and wasn't consumed, where God called Moses by name. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a thornbush. the word sounds like Sinai, the mountain this story leads to.

carryVoice: Your line: holy ground. The same dirt, and a voice that called his name. That's day three hundred sixty-nine.
